title: Cross-mode 5xx cascade during tenant failover — implement selective fast-fail and retry-sampling shim
creator: Alexandra Park
description:
Summary: During a tenant failover from Hosted -> Dedicated we observed a short-lived cascade of 5xx and timeouts that amplified through client retries and edge fanout. The incident affected three paying customers for ~18 minutes and caused elevated error rates across a subset of frontdoor proxies.

Problem statement: A failover (scheduled maintenance + capacity pressure) caused a cluster-level increase in tail latency. Edge proxies began triggering hedged requests and client SDK retries; those retries combined with request fanout to dedicated nodes produced transient KV cache thrashing and backend overload, producing 502/504 returns and ultimately a tenant-visible 5xx spike.

Goal: Deliver a low-risk, quick mitigation plus a durable patch that: (1) reduces retry amplification during cross-mode failovers, (2) gives a short-circuit fast-fail path for overloaded admission at the proxy layer, (3) preserves correctness and avoids customer-visible silent degradation. The fix should be safe to roll out to Hosted first, then Dedicated and Private.

Scope: Hosted API edge/proxy shim (fast-fail admission + retry-sampling), conservative rate-shed at dedicated admission controller, improved telemetry and synthetic tests to detect similar scenarios proactively.

Root cause (summary): 1) Admission controller used a combined queued length + slowpath threshold that did not account for rapid synchronized retriable retries from SDKs. 2) KV cache compaction policy caused hotspots under repeated prefix queries which increased backend CPU, slowing response generation. 3) Edge hedging combined with client retry backoff alignment caused microbursts.

Non-goals: Full KV rewrite, aggressive tenant eviction strategies, client SDK changes (we will notify SDK teams with guidance but not block this roll-out).
updates: 2026-03-08: Ticket created after post-incident triage meeting (Incident INC-2026-03-07-003). Assigned to Priya for mitigation + patch. Action: immediate telemetry review and identify short-term guardrail.
2026-03-09: Reproduced amplification pattern in staging using synthetic replay harness (link to replay). Confirmed hedged requests + aligned retry backoff produce >2x load compared to baseline.

2026-03-10: Implemented prototype fast-fail admission rule in edge proxy: when per-tenant in-flight requests exceed a percentile threshold and a short-latency-slowpath spike is detected, return a 429 with Retry-After for non-priority tenants. Smoke tests in canary passed.

2026-03-11: Began development of retry-sampling controller (0.1): instructs edge to sample client retries and convert excessive retries into controlled admission throttles instead of full fanout. PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/3245.

2026-03-12: Design review with PM and SRE: agreed to staged rollout (Hosted -> Dedicated control groups -> Private opt-in). Decision: default sampling rate 50% for non-enterprise tenants during detected failover windows; enterprise customers maintain priority fastpath.

2026-03-13: Added observability hooks: per-tenant retry-sample ratio, sampled-request queue time, and KV cache compaction counters to telemetry. Dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/tenant-failover/5xx-cascade.

2026-03-14: Integration tests show 40-60% reduction in transient 5xx under our synthetic microburst. Preparing rollout runbook and customer comms for all affected tenants. QA verification scheduled for 2026-03-16.
Note: updated_at reflects latest integration test validation and rollout readiness checks.
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout on hosted reduces peak 5xx rate by >=30% under synthetic microburst compared to baseline
Observed reduction in retry-amplification metric (tokens-per-second per-tenant) for sampled tenants
No regression in latency P50/P90 for priority enterprise tenants (less than 5% change)
Runbook created for SRE to toggle sampling and fast-fail and documented in Confluence
qa_plan: Create synthetic tenant scenarios with aligned retry clients in staging (use replay id 8902)
Run A/B test: baseline vs fast-fail+retry-sampling for 12h in canary pool, monitor 5xx, latency, and cost metrics
Manual exploratory: verify error semantics (429 Retry-After) are surfaced in SDK and documented
Regression tests: run full suite of streaming and batch generation tests to catch regressions
rollout_plan: Step 1 (Hosted canary - small): Deploy edge shim to 5% of Hosted edge nodes for low-risk tenants. Monitor for 24h. Metrics: 5xx spike amplitude, sampled retry ratio, queue time.
Step 2 (Hosted - broad): Expand to 50% of Hosted for non-enterprise tenants after green canary. Notify customers via status page and support.
Step 3 (Dedicated control): Apply admission controller config to Dedicated control group with conservative defaults; run controlled experiment with two large customers.
Step 4 (Private): Publish opt-in config and migration guidance for on-prem/VPC customers; include KMS/upgrade notes.
Rollback: Toggle sampling_rate=0 and disable fast-fail flag. Support playbook prepared for immediate rollback in 10 minutes.
Communication: Draft status page and customer-facing notes in support playbook (linked in Confluence).
postmortem_action_items: IA1: Tune KV cache compaction heuristics to avoid synchronized heavy compactions under repeat prefix queries (owner: infra-kv, estimate: 5)
IA2: SDK guidance: recommend jittered exponential backoff defaults; coordinate with SDK team for non-blocking rollout (owner: devexp, estimate: 3)
IA3: Add synthetic canary monitors that replay aligned-retry patterns hourly and alert if 5xx amplification > 20% (owner: SRE, estimate: 2)
IA4: Instrument admission controller with per-tenant slowpath counters and circuit triggers for more precise shedding (owner: serving-runtime, estimate: 4)
IA5: Update runbooks to include explicit steps for cross-mode failover and prioritized tenant whitelists (owner: SRE/Support, estimate: 1)
IA6: Post-rollout retrospective with customer success to review communications and SLA impacts (owner: PM, estimate: 1)
support_notes: Immediate mitigation: If customers report 5xx during a failover window, SRE should toggle edge.fastfail=false for the canary cohort to rule out false positives.
For priority customers: set tenant.priority=true to opt-out of sampling and preserve existing fastpath behavior.
Customer message draft available in Confluence under 'Cross-mode 5xx communications'
Hours to restore: Estimated 10-30 minutes for toggling flags and rolling hotfix to edge nodes; emergency contact: priya@redwood.ai
